### Observed differences

- In the later window the relative order of two activity groups is inverted. Earlier, one of A19, A21 or A24 (each in roughly 30–36 of 100 cases) ran before the A25/A29 part of the case, while A20, A22 and A23 (present in essentially every case) ran after it; in the later window A20/A22/A23 run first and A19/A21/A24 last. Pairwise order shares flipped almost completely: A20 precedes A25 in about 98 of 100 cases (previously about 0), A20 precedes A29 in essentially all cases (previously A29 preceded A20 in about 98), and A25 precedes A24 in about 38 of 100 (previously A24 preceded A25 in about 35). Positions match: A20/A22/A23 moved earlier (mean position about 0.64 → 0.38) and A19/A21/A24 later (about 0.36 → 0.67). [REL016, REL023, REL024, REL035, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]

- Successor profiles rewired consistently with that inversion. A19, A21 and A24 now lead to A30 in about 92–97 of 100 of their outgoing transitions (previously they led to A25 in about 93–97), while A20, A22 and A23 now lead to A25 in about 28–37 of their outgoing transitions (previously to A30 in about 29–37, now almost never). A29 now succeeds to A24/A21/A19 instead of A20/A23/A22, and A40 to A22/A20/A23 instead of A21/A19/A24. Direct-follow evidence agrees: A19 and A21 reach A30 at distance 1 in about 95 of 100 cases (essentially unobserved earlier), and A22/A23 reach A30 within five steps in about 199–200 cases earlier but only 1 afterwards. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, LAG018, LAG020, LAG022, LAG024]

- A08 is skipped far more often in the later window: it appears in about 29 of 100 cases versus about 64 before, and when present it sits later (mean position about 0.26 → 0.41). Its outgoing traffic concentrated on A16 fell from about 93 to 31 in 100, A15 now continues directly to A16 in about 88 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously about 61) and rarely reaches A08 (about 39 → 7), and cases containing A14 but not A08 rose from about 37 to 72 in 100. [OCC003, POS001, DIR002, DIR005, REL001]

- A04, A06 and A10 take part in roughly two to three times as many cases (about 7 → 21, 7 → 24 and 9 → 19 in 100) though they remain uncommon, with redistributed successors (A10 now leads most often to A46 and A15). The near-fixed sequences A43 → A44 and A45 → A46 loosened slightly (A44 about 96 → 85 of A43's outgoing transitions; A46 about 97 → 83 of A45's, with distance-2 A45 → A46 rising from about 3 to 16 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, DIR001, DIR003, DIR014, DIR015, LAG030]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the later window reflects a reordering of the middle of the process: the alternative group A19/A21/A24 and the always-present group A20/A22/A23 exchanged their places around the A25/A29 segment, so that A25 is now reached from A20/A22/A23 and A30 now follows A19/A21/A24, with A29 and A40 rewired in the matching direction. The support is direct and consistent: order shares between these activities reversed almost completely with about 200 cases behind each share, and the successor and position changes all point the same way. [REL023, REL024, REL030, REL035, DIR006, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, POS003, POS005, POS007]

The same windows also show A08 skipped in about 71 of 100 cases (previously about 36) with the A15 → A08 detour largely replaced by a direct A15 → A16 continuation, and A04/A06/A10 participation roughly tripled; these fit the reorganised flow, but many items summarise overlapping trace behaviour and should not be read as independent confirmations. [OCC003, DIR005, REL001, OCC001, OCC002, OCC004]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot exclude is a shift in the mix of case variants between the two windows rather than a structural modification: for the order reversal this is unlikely, since the shares are near-deterministic (about 97–100 in 100) in both windows, but for the participation changes in A08 and A04/A06/A10 a different case mix remains plausible, and the evidence supports no conclusion about causes. [OCC003, OCC001, REL023, REL031]
